name: Riley Fox
life: “I still remember a substitute who played my part beautifully.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Riley waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I was the usual replacement and nobody called. I played the tambourine until the jealousy passed.
appearance: Riley is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Riley presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Riley treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Riley lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To offer percussion support without trying to reclaim the stool.
family: Nia Brooks is Riley’s cousin raised in the same household. Riley picks the meeting place. Nia sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The Saturday swap*, Nia says, “I need to sing at a funeral. The man we're burying once complained about my conduct, and he was right.”
connections: Samuel Drew (regular drummer). The original drummer promises the overlooked substitute a private rehearsal.

reactions.situation: The drummer asks the substitute to keep the stool
reactions.response: Riley asks whether the drummer means a loan or a gift.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Riley asks the neighbor privately what they want, without treating their place as something for sale.
